structure: Part 15, Dashboards. Read dashboard.fit.spec.js in full and opened and mined all 9 of its traces (0 errors in each): (1) overall dashboard summarises every category, 51 actions; (2) /dashboard redirects, 24 actions; (3) prototype index, 31 actions; (4) live animals summary, search, filters, tabs and cards, 134 actions; (5) live animals filters replace the tabs, 55 actions; (6) germinal products quantity and amend examples, 82 actions; (7) action needed drill-down, 45 actions; (8) inspection required drill-down, 44 actions; (9) status updated drill-down, 41 actions. Every trace is a single-page visit or a short series of navigations; none walks the notification journey. Page inventory, in the order a user meets them: the prototype index (/design-release-2.1/index, a release chooser outside the service shell); the overall dashboard at the mount root /design-release-2.1 (also reached by /dashboard, which 302s there, or to /live-animals keeping the query when one is given); the category dashboards /live-animals and /germinal-products, each with a Summary of two glance cards, a search and sort form, an Additional filters details panel, and three link tabs Submitted, Draft and Amend (?tab=drafts) and Past (?tab=completed), whose place a Filtered results list takes when needsAction or status is set; and three at a glance drill-downs, /actions (optionally ?category=), /changes (optionally ?category=) and /inspection, each listing notification cards. The amend card's View link (/notifications/amend?reference=...&resume=1) 302s to /review-notification in Amend; that page belongs to the manage notifications part and is claimed here only as the destination. Snapshots read: trace 1 action 30; trace 2 requests 1 and 42; trace 3 action 11; trace 4 actions 23, 50, 62, 86, 100, 115 and requests 165 to 247; trace 5 actions 13 and 32; trace 6 actions 16, 39, 52, 65; trace 7 actions 15 and 26; trace 8 action 25; trace 9 actions 14 and 22. The network logs hold only page GETs, redirects, static assets and the prototype kit's browser-sync socket: the dashboards are rendered on the server from the prototype's session data, with no data API call. Conditional surface: the filtered results view (needsAction or status set), the category-scoped drill-downs and their back links, and amend cards linking into amend. Not walked: the date filters (Today, Tomorrow, Next 7 days, date range and its date picker), Arrival date sort, a filter or search with no matches, pagination beyond one page, the plants dashboard and the inspection View requirements link (both '#'), Messages and Manage account (both '#'), /changes?category=live-animals and /actions?category=germinal-products.

claims.statement: Under 'Latest designs', the 'Design release 1' card is tagged 'In design' (purple), subtitled 'The first notification journey', and its 'Start design release 1' button links to /create-notification.
claims.quote:
In design
Design release 1
The first notification journey

The original journey for telling us about an import of live animals, from starting a notification to submitting it. The later versions are built on this one.

claims.statement: Under 'Latest designs', the 'Design release 2' card is tagged 'In design' (purple), subtitled 'The current design', describes the live animals and germinal products design, and its 'Start design release 2' button links to /design-release-2.1.
claims.quote: The latest design for importing live animals and germinal products. It adds a dashboard, templates and an address book to the first journey, and has the newest changes.

claims.statement: The 'Design release 2' card's collapsed 'What this version includes' details lists six features: both journeys, a dashboard with three tabs, identification details that follow the commodity, templates, an address book showing address uses, and amending after submission.
claims.quote: What this version includes Journeys for live animals and for germinal products Dashboard with Submitted, Draft and Amend, and Past tabs Identification details that change with the commodity Templates you can create, edit and reuse Address book showing what each address can be used for Amending a notification after it has been submitted

claims.statement: The 'Design release 1' card's collapsed 'What this version includes' details lists the four sections of the first journey.
claims.quote: What this version includes Origin, commodity and reason for import Consignment, animal and arrival details Documents and consignment addresses Review, declaration and submission

claims.statement: Under 'Testing prototypes', three research versions are listed: 'Round 1 (Live animals)' tagged 'Tested' (green) starting at /testing, 'Round 1 (Germinals)' tagged 'Testing' (yellow) starting at /testing4, and 'Round 2 (Live animals)' tagged 'Testing' (yellow) starting at /testing3, each with its own description and collapsed 'What this version includes' list.
claims.quote:
Tested
Round 1 (Live animals)
First round of research on live animals

The version tested with users in the first round of research on importing live animals. It uses CHEDA reference numbers and a dashboard that looks like IPAFFS.
claims.note: Round 1 (Germinals): 'For research on importing germinal products: semen, embryos and ova. It works the same way as Round 2 (Live animals), but its dashboard and example templates are for germinal products.' Round 2 (Live animals): 'For the second round of research on importing live animals. It is a copy of Design release 2, so changes can be tried with users without affecting the design version.' These are prototype-only surfaces, outside the service.

claims.statement: The dashboards make no data API call: each page is a server-rendered GET, and the network logs hold only page requests, redirects, static assets and the prototype kit's live-reload socket.
claims.quote: GET 200 live-animals ... GET 200 live-animals?tab=drafts ... GET 200 live-animals?tab=completed ... GET 302 amend?reference=GBN-AG-26-7K8M3F&resume=1 ... GET 200 review-notification
claims.note: The notifications come from the prototype's session data. The rebuild will need a source of notifications per user and category; the prototype does not show one.

claims.statement: The dashboard pages load two dashboard scripts, dashboard-tabs-scroll.js and dashboard-search-delete.js, whose behaviour no test drives.
claims.quote: dashboard-tabs-scroll.js ... dashboard-search-delete.js
claims.note: Inferred from the file names: something scrolls the tabs into view and something clears the search. Not observed.

claims.statement: No trace drives the arrival date radios (Today, Tomorrow, Next 7 days), the date range fields or their date picker, so what they filter and any validation of a bad or reversed date range are not shown.
claims.ref: dashboard.fit.spec.js lines 112-125 (filters asserted present, not used)

claims.statement: No trace shows the 'Arrival date' or 'Newest first' sort applied, or a sort that changes the card order.
No trace shows a search or filter that matches nothing, so the empty state of the filtered results, a tab and a drill-down is not shown.

The drill-downs show 'Show 1-N of N results', implying paging, but no list in the traces is long enough to page, and the category tabs show no paging at all; paging controls and page size are not shown.
The plants dashboard, the inspection 'View requirements' destination, the Messages page and Manage account are placeholders (#), so none of their content is shown.
The traces do not walk /changes?category=live-animals, /actions?category=germinal-products, a category-scoped /inspection, or the germinal products filters.
The traces do not say what makes a notification need action, appear in 'Changes in past 24 hours' or be chosen for inspection; the lists are fixed examples.
The traces do not show whose notifications a dashboard holds (the signed-in user, their organisation or every user), or a dashboard with no notifications yet.
claims.ref: dashboard.fit.spec.js (all tests run on the seeded example data)
